dedupe_keys.name: 5g energy lab simulator software defined modelling of energy consumption and resilience scenarios in a 5g laboratory testbed

description: The software author publishes a parametric simulator for power use and service quality in a software-defined 5G laboratory. Zenodo provides a ZIP and Ukrainian-language README; the README states MIT for code while repository metadata state CC BY 4.0 for the deposit. A Python notebook and standalone script model a 5G core, user attachments, radio activity, traffic and CPU load. Eleven scenarios include idle, high traffic, denial-of-service overload, base-station failure, recovery and energy saving. The model exports per-second power, throughput, latency, packet loss and energy-intensity series. It can test digital-network energy and resilience assumptions. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this simulator. Coverage is a synthetic lab architecture with no physical radios or power meter. A limitation is that power coefficients are starting estimates awaiting calibration after a real laboratory exists. The script was not executed and its metrics were not independently measured.
